title: fix(metadata-protocol)!: the read naming no bundle member addresses the canonical member alone, as ?member=en-US and /published do
body:
Fixes #34682

Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — no page under `skills/**` or `content/docs/**` teaches the read naming no member of a bundle that has no canonical member; `content/docs/references` prints the selector sentence this change now follows, and the ADR-0146 paragraph of `skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md` names members only at a base or a package address. No taught sentence moves.

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:邮件模板这类“分成员”的元数据，按名字读且不指定成员时，现在只读规范成员 `en-US`;如果这个模板根本没有 `en-US`,普通读、`/layers`、执行读都答 404,和 `?member=en-US`、`/published` 一致。
- 为什么改:规范写明“不指定成员 = 规范成员，写出 `en-US` 是同一个请求”,但旧代码对没有 `en-US` 的模板会悄悄返回另一种语言(如 `fr-FR`),同一请求两种写法得到 200 和 404;只存了 `fr-FR` 行的模板甚至在重启前后答案不同。
- 风险与回滚：只影响“没有 `en-US` 成员的邮件模板，不带 `?member=` 读”这一种请求，由 200 变 404;邮件发送走列表读，不受影响;Studio 列表按行带 `?member=` 打开，不受影响。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- 先看:`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-item-reads.ts`(成员判断那一行)、`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-layered-reads.ts`(删掉的无成员回退)、`packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.bundle-without-canonical-member-bare-read-absent.ts`(升级说明)。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime exec vitest run src/domains/meta-bundle-member-one-request.test.ts`,预期 1 个测试通过。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地(这次由 200 变 404 已按收窄申报并补 ADR-0087 登记，契约审查档 L2 由席位安排)。

## What changes

The governing text is the member selector's declared contract, `BUNDLE_MEMBER_SELECTOR_DESCRIPTION` in `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`, which every by-name request's `member` carries:

> "Absent, the canonical member (`en-US` for `email_template`), which is what a bare-name read answers; naming the canonical value is the same request. [...] A well-formed member with nothing stored or shipped answers as that door answers an absent item."

The two pairs the card names are both this one request. Measured on `origin/main` d947a93cf8, through `HttpDispatcher.dispatch` on a booted kernel, for a bundle that ships or stores no `en-US` member:

| request | `main` | this PR |
|:--|:--|:--|
| A ships `fr-FR` only: plain read | 200, the `fr-FR` member | 404 `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` |
| same: `?member=en-US` | 404 `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` |
| same: `/published` | 404 `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` |
| same: `/layers` / `/layers?member=en-US` | 200 `fr-FR` / 404 | 404 / 404 |
| same: execution read / with `en-US` | the `fr-FR` item / null | null / null |
| same, `?package=A` naming no member (also with a dependent's `en-US` row stored) | 200 `fr-FR` | 404 `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` |
| package-less `fr-FR` row only: plain read | 404 before a restart, 200 `fr-FR` after it | 404 on both sides |
| same: `?member=en-US`, `/published`, `/layers` | 404 on both sides | 404 on both sides |

The producer of the stray member is the registry's bare-name read (`SchemaRegistry.getItem` with no member), which still answers a bundle with no canonical member with its first member. That is the registry's own documented contract for its other callers, so it is left alone. The by-name reads now ask for the member this request addresses:

- `readMetaItem` (the plain read and the execution read): the code layers' answer is kept only when it is the addressed member, the canonical one when none was named. Before this PR that check ran only for a named member.
- `getMetaItemLayered`: the same check on the registry answer, and the member-less artifact lookup added for the #34441 cell 1 case is removed. For a type with no members, that lookup repeated the artifact lookup above it with the same arguments, so removing it changes nothing for such a type.
- `registryMemberServedAt` (the base-address step of `readMetaItem`): naming no member, it falls back to the base's own canonical member only. Before, it fell back to the base's first shipped member. CI on 3cb177c571 found this path (Test Core, `packages/objectql/src/protocol-bundle-member-base-address.test.ts`): `?package=BASE` naming no member, and the read naming no package once a dependent stores `en-US`, still served the base's `fr-FR`.
- `resolveBundleMemberSelector`'s docblock states the canonical-member rule. The orphan-report comment in the layered read is updated to match.
- One ADR-0087 semantic entry, `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.bundle-without-canonical-member-bare-read-absent.ts`, registers the narrowing. It follows the shape of `18.shipped-base-dependent-canonical-row-not-published.ts`. The registry is generated from it (`gen:migration-registry`, gitignored output), and the changeset carries `adr-0087: registered bundle-without-canonical-member-bare-read-absent` with a BREAKING banner. No key, stored shape or export moves.

Unchanged: a bundle that ships or stores `en-US`, every named member, and every type with no members. `/published` is unchanged. It takes no selector and already read the canonical member.

**Narrowing:** this narrows what a caller receives. One served answer becomes 404: the read naming no member of a bundle with no canonical member. The seat ruled the `(narrowing)` arm (L1 rework round 1; revised claim 6953428610), following PR #34644. So the title takes `!`, and the changeset takes the BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 registration above. A contract-review-tier L2 is owed for the narrowing and the `packages/spec/src/**` path.

## Tests

- New `packages/runtime/src/domains/meta-bundle-member-one-request.test.ts` boots a kernel on a file database and reads before and after a restart.
  - Pair 2: `?member=en-US` equals the read naming no member, including the whole served envelope, on the plain read, `/layers` and the execution read. Covered for a shipped `fr-FR`-only bundle and a stored `fr-FR`-only row (both 404/null), and for a shipped `en-US` bundle and a stored `en-US` row (both served).
  - Pair 1: `/published` and the plain read give the same answer for those no-canonical bundles (404) and for a stored canonical row (200, same document). `/published?member=en-US` is a 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR`.
  - CONTROL, a type with no members (`dashboard`): `?member=en-US` is refused 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR` on the plain read, `/layers` and the execution read. A stored row is served alike by the plain read and `/published`.
  - Every refusal asserts `status` and `code`.
- `meta-disabled-holder-served-stack.test.ts` cell 1: the CONTROL (no D row) moves to the canonical answer (plain read, `/layers` 404, execution read null). The comment above S1 that said no shipped CONTROL could be pinned is corrected.
- `protocol.lookup-artifact-item-call-sites.test.ts`: the removed `getMetaItemLayered` site leaves the ledger (26 to 25 sites).
- `packages/objectql/src/protocol-bundle-member-base-address.test.ts`: the no-canonical case now pins 404 on the read naming no member, at the base's address and naming no package, the same as `?member=en-US`. The base's `fr-FR`, named, is still the base's, and the dependent's `en-US` is still served at its own address. The new runtime pin also compares `?package=A` with and without `?member=en-US` for the shipped bundles.

## Acceptance notes

- Not the member selector's: `/published` answers 404 for an item that only code ships, bundled or not. The plain read serves 200 for the same item. The new test pins this for `dashboard` and `email_template` alike, and the existing `SPECIMENS` pin in `meta-disabled-holder-served-stack.test.ts` already holds it for a code-only agent and dashboard. So `/published` and the plain read give one answer wherever a published document exists or none does, which is the scope of the card's pair 1. This is an observation and was not filed.
- The registry's bare-name read (`registry-items.ts`) keeps answering a bundle with no canonical member with its first member, for its other callers. No by-name door takes that answer now. Changing the registry would widen the change to `@objectstack/objectql`, and nothing here asks for it.
- The new pin is a new file, as the dispatch named it. The selector's existing harness, `protocol.bundle-member-selector.test.ts`, is a pure unit test with no doors, and the `/published` door lives in `packages/runtime`.
